To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the bronchial epithelium from mild asthmatic subjects, but not normal controls, constitutively secretes IL-5 and -13 in response to allergens, and that this response requires B7/CD-28 costimulation.
allergen induces the secretion of IL-13 and IL-5 by bronchial mucosal tissue of asthmatics but not of control subjects.
the allergen-induced secretion and expression of IL-4 and IL-13 by cultured bronchial tissue is inhibited by CTLA-4-Ig.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that control the production of IL5 and IL-4 and the role that IL-4 and IL-5 play in the development of asthma.
the cellular interactions required for cytokine production in asthmatic airway inflammation.
the cellular interactions required for cytokine secretion in asthmatic and normal bronchial mucosal tissue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
allergen induces the secretion of the Th2-type cytokines IL-5 and, to a lesser extent, IL-13 by the bronchus of atopic asthmatc subjects.

the expression of IL5 and IL13 in the bronchial epithelial cells of atopic asthmatice patients can be stimulated in an ex vivo system by the addition of allergen and is inhibited by the fusion of the CTLA4Ig.
the allergen-induced secretion by bronchially derived T cells of IL-5 is dependent on B7 costimulation, whereas IL-13 production is independent of B7 costimulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bronchial epithelium is not a source of IL-5 or IL-13 in response to allergens.
the expression of IL5 and IL13 in the bronchial tissue of atopic subjects can be induced by allergen stimulation.
B7 costimulation is a key event in allergen-induced cytokine secretion by bronchially derived cells from mild asthmatic subjects but not from nonasthmatic subjects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
B7/CD80 costimulation is required to produce IL-5 and/or IL-13 by the allergen-stimulated bronchial tissue of atopic asthma subjects.
allergen-induced secretion from the bronchial explant cultures is mediated through the B7 costimulatory pathway and requires CD80 (B71) or CD86 (B72) for the expression of IL5 and IL13.
allergen stimulation of the asthmatic lung induces the expression of Th2 cytokine mRNA and protein.
